question: What do we call a failure to provide standard care that accidentally leads to patient harm?
explanation: Negligence happens when someone fails to give the ordinary care expected of a professional, causing unintentional harm. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of professional misconduct rather than a simple clinical mistake?

options.A: Failing to monitor fetal heart rate during the first stage of labor
options.B: Miscalculating the dose of an oxytocin infusion due to fatigue
options.C: Accidentally dropping a sterile instrument on the floor during delivery
options.D: Demanding illegal unofficial fees from a patient to access delivery services

explanation: Asking for unauthorized fees is unethical and violates the professional rules set by the council. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which body has the legal power to discipline midwives and set practice standards in Nigeria?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the legal authority that oversees nursing and midwifery education, registration, and discipline in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the main reason for having strict legal and regulatory rules in midwifery?

options.A: Limiting the total number of practicing midwives in urban centers
options.B: Safeguarding the health and safety of the general public
options.C: Protecting individual midwives from civil lawsuits
options.D: Ensuring uniform salary structures across all health facilities

explanation: All health regulations exist primarily to protect patients who receive healthcare services. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a situation that usually leads to negligence claims?

options.A: Administering an incorrect dose of a powerful uterotonic drug
options.B: Failing to monitor the fetal heart rate regularly during active labor
options.C: Timely referral of an obstructed labor case to a specialist hospital
options.D: Leaving a woman in active labor completely unattended for hours

explanation: Promptly referring a complicated case to a higher center is good clinical practice that prevents negligence claims. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h3)

question: A midwife sees baby warning signs on the monitor but waits until her shift ends to call the doctor. What legal risk is she taking?

options.A: Professional negligence due to delayed action and poor monitoring
options.C: Practicing outside the approved scope of nursing

explanation: Ignoring clear signs of fetal distress and delaying help is a direct breach of the duty of care. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the very first step when someone makes a formal complaint of professional misconduct against a midwife?

options.A: Arrest and detention of the midwife by the police
options.B: Receipt and documentation of the written petition
options.C: Public announcement of the charges in national newspapers
options.D: Immediate withdrawal of the midwife's practicing license

explanation: The process always starts by receiving and logging a formal written complaint before any investigation begins. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why must an accused midwife receive a copy of the petition and a chance to write a defense?

options.A: To bypass the need for an investigative panel altogether
options.B: To give the union time to organize a strike action before the trial
options.C: To allow the midwife enough time to destroy unfavorable hospital records
options.D: To uphold the fundamental principle of fair hearing and natural justice

explanation: Natural justice means anyone accused of an offense must know the allegations and get a fair chance to defend themselves. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h4)

question: Who sits on the Nursing and Midwifery Disciplinary Tribunal alongside legal professionals?

options.A: Civil rights lawyers and human rights activists
options.B: Elected political representatives from the local government
options.C: Experienced senior nursing and midwifery practitioners
options.D: Hospital accountants and human resource managers

explanation: The tribunal includes senior peers who understand clinical standards, working alongside legal experts. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h5)

question: What happens right after a tribunal finds a midwife guilty of gross professional misconduct?

options.A: The midwife is automatically promoted to a senior administrative rank
options.B: The affected patient is appointed as the new head of the nursing unit
options.C: Appropriate sanctions are applied, such as suspension or removal from the register
options.D: The case is permanently closed without any record kept in the registry

explanation: Guilty verdicts lead to professional penalties, which can include suspension or removing the practitioner's name from the official register. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is writing down care notes right away so important in midwifery?

options.A: It is required primarily for hospital statistical billing purposes
options.B: It allows doctors to bypass writing their own clinical notes
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will never be sued by patients
options.D: It serves as primary legal evidence of the care provided to the patient

explanation: Accurate, written records are treated by courts as the most reliable proof of what happened during care. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h6)

question: A midwife forgets to record a medication dose and squeezes the entry into a past date. What is the legal meaning of this?

options.A: It is standard administrative practice as long as the drug was given
options.B: It constitutes falsification of records, which worsens legal liability
options.C: It is acceptable provided the head of department countersigns it
options.D: It is a minor clerical error with no professional consequences

explanation: Backdating or altering records after an incident destroys credibility and is treated as serious fraud during investigations. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of professional indemnity insurance for a practicing midwife?

options.A: Providing financial protection and legal defense support in civil lawsuits
options.B: Replacing the need to register annually with the regulatory council
options.C: Covering the cost of personal medical treatment during illness
options.D: Guaranteeing automatic promotion and salary increments every year

explanation: Indemnity insurance protects midwives against the high costs of legal defense and damages if a patient sues. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which proactive practice helps a midwife avoid professional misconduct or negligence claims?

options.A: Avoiding documentation to prevent patients from reading their charts
options.B: Delegating all complex deliveries entirely to untrained assistants
options.C: Refusing to communicate with patient relatives during emergencies
options.D: Practicing strictly within evidence-based guidelines and established scope

explanation: Following approved protocols and staying within your trained scope ensures safe care and prevents legal trouble. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h7)
